name: Pembrolizumab Monotherapy (KEYNOTE-048), First-Line Recurrent or Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma, PD-L1 CPS at least 1
disease: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (non-nasopharyngeal)

biomarkers.PD_L1_CPS: at least 1 (CPS >= 1 required for first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy)
biomarkers.note: Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers v2.2026, SYST-A 4 of 7, first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy is limited to tumors that express PD-L1 with a combined positive score (CPS) at least 1 (category 1). The Discussion (MS-56) confirms pembrolizumab alone is a first-line option for PD-L1 positive (CPS >= 1) disease based on KEYNOTE-048; the OS benefit for monotherapy was seen in the CPS >= 20 and CPS >= 1 populations. Combined positive score is assessed by PD-L1 IHC.

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: PD-L1 positive, combined positive score (CPS) at least 1
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, SYST-A 4 of 7 (Recurrent, Unresectable, or Metastatic Disease, First-Line Preferred: Pembrolizumab for tumors that express PD-L1 with CPS >= 1, category 1)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: recurrent, unresectable, or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma with no surgical or radiotherapy option
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, SYST-A 4 of 7 header (Recurrent, Unresectable, or Metastatic Disease with no surgery or RT option)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: non-nasopharyngeal primary (oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, glottic or supraglottic larynx, ethmoid or maxillary sinus, occult primary); nasopharynx follows a separate systemic-therapy pathway (NASO-B)
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, SYST-A 1 of 7 (Principles of Systemic Therapy for Non-Nasopharyngeal Cancers header)

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
provenance.locator: Discussion MS-59 (pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks; FDA-approved alternate 400 mg every 6 weeks); indication SYST-A 4 of 7 (first-line, CPS >= 1, category 1)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, Discussion MS-59. Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV flat dose on day 1 every 21 days. Source-stated alternate schedule: 400 mg IV every 42 days (approved across adult indications). Flat milligram dosing (basis flat), not mg/kg. Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

regimen.cycles: until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; alternate schedule 400 mg every 42 days
supportiveCare: Immune-related adverse event surveillance for pembrolizumab (thyroid, hepatic, pulmonary, colitis, dermatologic, endocrine).
Antiemetic prophylaxis not routinely required for single-agent checkpoint inhibitor (minimal emetic risk).

monitoring: immune-related toxicity screen (TSH/free T4, LFTs, glucose, cortisol as indicated) during pembrolizumab
imaging every 2 to 3 cycles in the recurrent/metastatic setting (Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, SYST-A 1 of 7 general principles)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold pembrolizumab and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; obtain clinical review before rechallenge.

core.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22nd ed.
core.locator: Head and Neck Cancer chapter, Recurrent/Metastatic disease (lines 88276 to 88304): PD-1 inhibitors pembrolizumab and nivolumab established in recurrent or metastatic disease; benefit correlates with PD-L1 expression

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
guideline.locator: SYST-A 4 of 7 (Recurrent, Unresectable, or Metastatic Disease, First-Line Preferred: Pembrolizumab for PD-L1 CPS >= 1, category 1); dosing Discussion MS-59; KEYNOTE-048 Discussion MS-55 to MS-56

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy (KEYNOTE-048) in recurrent, unresectable, or metastatic non-nasopharyngeal head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Serves the squamous-cell head and neck sites (oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, glottic and supraglottic larynx, ethmoid and maxillary sinus, occult primary; reference sites #32 to 39 and #41), not nasopharynx (separate NASO-B pathway) and not salivary gland (#40, separate protocol). Pembrolizumab flat 200 mg IV every 21 days (alternate 400 mg every 42 days) is sourced to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026 Discussion MS-59; the first-line indication and the PD-L1 CPS at least 1 gate (category 1) are from SYST-A 4 of 7 and Discussion MS-55 to MS-56. Setting recurrent/metastatic, palliative intent, first-line. Flat milligram dosing recorded (basis flat), not mg/kg. No numeric field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
